description: Solo team from Dubai. I'm a grade 10 student and web developer working on Baseline, a health monitoring app that compares each astronaut's daily readings to their own Earth baseline and flags drift over mission days. Skills: web development, UI design, HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
summary: Baseline is a health monitoring tool that helps astronauts check their own health during long missions. Instead of comparing readings to generic textbook ranges, it compares each astronaut's daily readings to their own Earth baseline, recorded before launch, and flags drift over mission days. A clickable body map shows each body system as green, amber or red. Tapping a zone explains what it does, how spaceflight affects it, and what to do now. Red results show a "Flag flight surgeon" button so the ground team can step in. This matters because on long missions astronauts are far from doctors, and small changes that build up slowly are easy to miss.
details:
Baseline tracks six indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood sugar, sleep hours and mood. The astronaut records a baseline once before launch, then does a daily check-in that takes about 30 seconds. The app calculates the percentage drift from that baseline and maps it to body zones: heart, brain and mood, bones and muscles, metabolism and sleep. Trend charts show the last 7 days with the personal baseline as a dashed line, so slow drift is easy to see. A streak counter keeps the habit going, and a built-in guide explains how to take each measurement.

It is built as a single HTML, CSS and JavaScript file with no backend, so it works offline, which matters when communication with Earth is delayed. Data is stored on the device. The drift thresholds are illustrative for the prototype; in a real version they would be set with flight surgeons. Next steps are wearable sensor sync and a crew dashboard for flight surgeons. The prototype code was generated with AI assistance (Claude) and reviewed and tested by me. This is a prototype, not a medical device.
